newsitem.title: CHINA: China, U.S. plan textile talks in Beijing.
newsitem.headline: China, U.S. plan textile talks in Beijing.

text.p: China and the United States have agreed to hold another round of talks this month aimed at hammering out a new agreement on textile trade, the official Xinhua news agency said on Thursday.
The bilateral pact had been scheduled to expire on December 31 last year but was extended until January 31 amid progress on renewing the 1994 accord.

The talks, slated to begin in Beijing on January 27, would also cover U.S. penalties imposed on imports of Chinese textiles and China's threat to retaliate, the news agency said in a report quoting a spokesman of the Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation.
Washington announced in September $19 million in penalties on imports of textiles from China, accusing Chinese companies of shipping goods through third countries to evade U.S. import quotas.

China had planned to impose retaliatory curbs on imports of some U.S. textiles, farm goods and alcoholic drinks on December 10 but it agreed to extend the deadline until the end of this month to give the two sides more time for negotiation.
During the previous round of talks in Washington last month, the U.S. side said it would re-examine its decision to reduce quotas for Chinese textiles, Xinhua said.
